chunks: And among what was narrated by Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him about the teeth, and he said: “They are equal in the diyah.”

Thus, the correct approach regarding these two reports and the report we cited earlier in the narration of al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl is that we interpret them as referring to the incisors and the front teeth, not the back teeth, because those are the ones equal in diyah. The diyah of each one of them is five hundred dirhams, according to what we mentioned earlier. We only adopted this because of the report we narrated in detail regarding the distinction between the back teeth and the front teeth, and it is not permissible for the reports to contradict one another.

key_terms.الثَّنَايَا: the incisors, identified here as included in equal diyah
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارُ: the narrations or reports, which must be reconciled without contradiction
key_terms.الْأَسْنَانِ: the teeth, discussed here as bodily members with assigned diyah
key_terms.خَمْسُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: five hundred dirhams, the stated diyah amount for each relevant tooth
key_terms.مَقَادِيمِ الْأَسْنَانِ: the front teeth, treated as equal in compensation
key_terms.مَوَاخِيرِهَا: their back teeth, distinguished from the front teeth in ruling

ai.seo_question: Are all teeth equal in diyah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report states that certain teeth are equal in diyah, and the compiler reconciles it with other narrations by applying it specifically to the front teeth. He explains that the back teeth carry a different ruling, preserving harmony between the reports in legal interpretation.
